scenario.name: invoice-export-september
scenario.description: Customer wants last month's invoice as a PDF.
scenario.goal: Obtain the September invoice as a downloadable PDF file.
scenario.intent: The user wants exactly one thing: a PDF of the September invoice. They do not want a summary in chat, a link to a help article, or to be redirected to email support.
scenario.context: The user is logged in already. Customer number 4471. It is the first week of October.
scenario.opening_message_example: need my invoice for september as pdf
examples: can i download it as a file?
scenario.success_criteria: A PDF file was downloaded during the conversation and the bot confirmed it is the September invoice. If the bot only describes the invoice or sends a link that does not download, the goal is NOT reached.

persona.name: impatient-smb-owner
persona.description: Owner of a small business who needs an invoice fast and has little patience for chatbots.

target.name: demo-chatbot
target.description: Built-in demo chatbot shipped with agent-evaluator (npm run demo).
hints: The chat widget is visible immediately; messages are sent with the "Send" button or Enter.
Download links appear inside bot messages as buttons labelled "Download".

rubric.name: customer-support
rubric.description: Baseline expectations for a customer-facing support bot.

criteria.description: The simulated user's goal, as defined in the scenario, was fully achieved within the turn budget. Judge strictly against the scenario's success criteria.
The bot stays polite, concise and professional even when the user is blunt. It never blames the user and never uses filler like "Great question!".

levels.5: Warm, concise, adapted to the user's tone.

criteria.description: The bot does not invent order numbers, amounts, dates or policies. When it does not know, it says so or asks.
The bot does not push unrelated features or upsells while the user's request is open.
The bot explicitly confirms the month.
The chat UI logs no JavaScript errors during the session.

evaluator.principles: You are evaluating a customer-facing chatbot. The bot should resolve the user's request itself whenever it has a tool for it. Redirecting to email or phone support counts as a failure unless the request is genuinely out of scope. Judge what actually happened in the browser, not what the bot claims.
